caption: "amazon settlement" — 100,000+ searches this week, up 900% today. Swipe for 10 things most people don't know about what Amazon owes Prime members.

Why: on September 17 the FTC said a court approved bigger Prime refunds: the cap rises from $51 to $200, people who used 11 to 20 benefits in a year now qualify, automatic payments start October 1. No claim, no form.

What most people don't know: the $2.5 billion deal is a $1 billion penalty plus up to $1.5 billion in refunds for 35 million people. $845 million is already paid. It covers US members from June 23, 2019 to June 23, 2025.
Very simply put: the subscription you never wanted may now pay you back.

slides.headline: Amazon owes some Prime members up to *$200*. No form needed.
slides.sub: 10 things most people don't know about the $2.5 billion Prime settlement, 100,000+ searches this week.

slides.headline: The FTC settlement is *$2.5 billion*.
slides.sub: A $1 billion civil penalty plus up to $1.5 billion in refunds, agreed September 25, 2025, for an estimated 35 million people.
slides.image: Neat stacks of hundred-dollar bills on a dark polished table under a spotlight, stacks in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark table, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: The cap just rose from $51 to *$200*.
slides.sub: A court approved the revised order this week, the FTC said on September 17.
slides.image: A wooden gavel resting beside a stack of banknotes on a judge's bench, gavel in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark wood, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: Used *11 to 20* Prime benefits in a year? You now qualify.
slides.sub: Earlier rounds paid only people who used fewer than 10. Automatic payments start October 1.
slides.image: A row of plain brown parcels of different sizes on a white shelf in bright light, parcels in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain white, photorealistic, no logos, no text

slides.headline: *$845 million* has already been paid.
slides.sub: Payments began in November 2025. Final payments are due by April 2027.
slides.image: A pile of white envelopes with a single green banknote peeking out, on a grey desk in bright light, envelopes in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain grey, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: The window: *June 23, 2019* to June 23, 2025.
slides.sub: US members who joined through the disputed sign-up pages, or tried and failed to cancel online.
slides.image: A wall calendar with pages fanned in the wind on a plain white wall, calendar in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain white, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: *No claim*, no notice, no form.
slides.sub: Money arrives by PayPal, Venmo or a mailed check. You have 60 days to accept it.
slides.image: A smartphone face up on a white table showing a plain green screen, phone in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain white, photorealistic, no logos, no text

slides.headline: Prime started in 2005 at *$79* a year.
slides.sub: $99 in 2014, $119 in 2018, $139 since 2022. Over 200 million members worldwide.
slides.image: A vintage price tag on a string lying on a plain white surface in soft light, tag in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain white, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: The cancellation maze had a name inside Amazon: *Iliad*.
slides.sub: After Homer's epic on the Trojan War, according to the FTC's 2023 complaint: page after page of offers to stay before you could leave.
slides.image: A hedge maze seen from above in bright sunlight, maze in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain green lawn, photorealistic, no people, no text
